 Mominul ruled out with concussion, Jaker named replacement
 Published : 30 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 30 October 2026, 15:33
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 PHOTO: FIROZ AHMED 
 Bangladesh batter Mominul Haque has been ruled out for the remainder of the first Test against West Indies after suffering a concussion while fielding on day three at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium today. 
 Jaker Ali Anik was brought in as Mominul’s concussion substitute after the left-hander was unable to continue following a head injury during the visitors’ first innings.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 The incident occurred in the 78th over when Mominul attempted to take a catch at short-leg off Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s bowling but failed to hold on to Joshua Bishop’s effort. He fell face-first onto the ground and appeared to be in considerable pain before being taken off the field.
 Mominul’s absence became a concern when Bangladesh began their second innings. With Tanzid Hasan dismissed for a duck, skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto came in at number three instead of Mominul.
 Shadman Islam (13) and Towhid Hridoy (0) soon followed, leaving Bangladesh in early trouble. After Shanto’s dismissal, with the Tigers struggling at 33 for four, Jaker came out to bat despite not being part of the original playing XI.
 The Bangladesh Cricket Board later confirmed the substitution in a media release.
 “Mominul Haque had suffered a head injury while fielding in the 78th over of the West Indies first innings. As he has shown signs of concussion, he has been replaced by Jaker Ali Anik as the concussion sub for the remainder of the match,” BCB physio Bayjedul Islam Khan said in the statement.
 Mominul became only the third Bangladesh batter to be replaced due to concussion in Test cricket.
 Jaker, who last played a Test for Bangladesh in June 2025, joined the side at a difficult juncture
